summary: The team is juggling immediate IT recovery from an Outlook lockout while advancing key marketing initiatives—Asia Start, Intelligent China, and the knowledge website redesign—with critical follow-ups due this week.
summaryDetail: Right now, the most urgent issue is resolving the Outlook account lockout: the team must delete and re-login to update passwords across devices, check mobile Outlook, and confirm with JSB that the backend lock is lifted. In parallel, the knowledge website redesign is nearing a feedback milestone—Joseph needs to share his HTML design, and he, Julie, and the speaker must meet for half an hour to provide specific feedback, while integrating more articles and the BCI index banner into the knowledge section. The Global Marketing Strategy push continues, with Joseph drafting target areas and focus, the team providing a conversion tracking brief, and Joseph analyzing participant profiles to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China (with Berkeley as a possible third). Looking ahead, several time-sensitive items are due: Ira must review and edit the invitation email for Professor Hong Wang for the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum, TIAN Xuefang must confirm the SproutVideo annual subscription renewal, Ira and Julie need to discuss the Macrobond Mei Moses Art Indices opportunity, and Ira will follow up with Asia Start participants for interviews, including potential interviews with three BCG partners. Additionally, Ira should draft a Chinese email to Zongchao regarding CKGSB engagements at the Sino-Swiss Economic Forum, and DONG Kunyu must check and get back to Ira on that forum.
